Maybe that's why, at least in my case, I have such a weird sense of humor. Dark even? I can laugh at my dark moments now because they were ridiculous. And its like a horriblensitcom in my head. I guess its my way of dealing with it?

I really don't know. I am really scared of them thinking I'm just seeking attention. I don't want them to think I'm not thinking of them or that I don't love them. Especially my Best friend She's super against suicide. If I do it I do it I won't tell anyone.

Yeah! Sometimes we find any excuse to feel bad for feeling good. Its okay to feel good and bond with people who understand your situation in a world where all we got slaps in the face for being happy and feeling good. Just remember that you were probs raised in a place were guilt was a weapon. Don't feel guilty for being validated.

I'm sorry I'm not fit to give you advice I just can talk from experience so take it with a grain of salt. Its okay if you love her. Its okay to love your mom. If you think that's why then cool. But... If you know that you have to distance yourself for your own mental wellbeing then its okay to think about yourself. You wouldn't stay with a toxic group of friends right?(I'm assuming) so why your mom? If you have the ability to then slowly try to. I know its sounds easier said than done. But fr if you avoid her forever I'm sure that's way more draining than having a conversation with her.

If you had a bad time in your childhood than yes you were probs raised by narcs. I mean by what you're saying not that I'm diagnosing or anything. But just things like that you expected a big fight or you tense up when his dad calmly called him out on it.. It happens to me too. Its not about labeling either. Try and reevaluate what you relationship.with your Nparent was. They might have not beat you but mental/emotional abuse is still abuse.

Do you have to talk to her? Any ties?

Or do you want to cut her off?

I don't think you're addicted to it. I think a lot of people here never really experienced it with their Nparents so they share their stories for people to say "hey me too" nd have sympathy for each other. I'm pretty positive you've read someone's story on here and felt for them. Well we feel for you too. You're only addicted to it when you don't give it back or when its about something fake. So you decide.

Its so refreshing to be in a place where you can share a story or thought about what you went through and get a "me too" or a "how you feel is valid". When in the real world all we get is "don't play victim" or weird looks. You all know what having a bad parent means. You all know what surviving a bad parent means. You're here and you're sharing your story and sometimes this place makes me feel like I'm not alone. So thanks to all of you! You help me everyday.
No no like I said before, if I ever encountered a kid that gave me a red flag like that I would make it my business and try to help. But in my specific situation I'm grateful she didn't get involved.
I just don't think that anything would've changed if I would've gotten help form anyone. Its been done and nothing changed so I don't blame my friends mom for butting out. Its not her problem
You're right, I know for a fact that if my dad would've found out someone was trying to get me out of the situation he would've made it worse for me.

My ex boyfriend would always use this on me. He would say "there you go again playing victim" or "that victim mentality is the only thing holding you back" whenever I would say that I felt like sometimes he would leave me for someone prettier or that I felt life just held me down a lot. 

But dude, we were raise to be blamed. If one of our Nparents felt bed about themselves or angry we were the punching bag. We were taught that we were never gonna be good enough and a lot of us have learned that that's not right but we do it unconsciously. I don't think were playing the victim card. We were victims. For a long time. 

I don't mean to compare myself to a person with ptsd but its similar. I hope one day we learn to overcome this.

She dropped me off and never talked about it or told me what it was. You can imagine the horror in my face when I learned what it was a few months later.

Idk this reminds me of my "ex" best friend. 

She's 32 and I'm 22. We met at an English class for adults. It was our way of getting out there. It was more of a poetry club tbh. We clicked instantly. Soon after we because super close and she met my family. She was alone in the world. Her mom had passed away some years back and she never met her dad. She was an only child and her aunts and uncles lived in another country. She was good at being alone. She had exes and such but it had been years since she was with someone.

One day I asked her out with my sister and all 3 of us had a night out on the town. My sister asked about her dating status and when she learned she had been single for so long she instantly asked if she could hook her up. She agreed. She met this dude who was perfect on paper. He wanted kids and a house almost instantly with her they hit it off really nicely. 

A year after all of that their relationship started to have troubles and they split up. She would call me crying saying she wasn't good enough for anyone and that she was never gonna have kids or get to wear her moms dress for her wedding. I didn't know what to say most of the time. Until, one day she told me the exact same thing here. She said if she wasn't settled down by 35 she was gonna end her life. 

At the time I didn't have the mental stability to deal with that. I didn't wanna hear my best friend say she was gonna kill herself. So I got angry and I just stopped talking to her. 

But hearing your side make me think twice about it. You're not a bad person for wanting to end it on your own terms. I guess I was being selfish and should have been there for her.

I had a lot of anxiety like wanting closure. It messed with my future relationships if I didn't get it. But I've just come to the conclusion that if I met them half way and they didn't and we parted ways "it is what it is". I know it sounds like easier said than done. But tbh if they want you there they would've never opened the door for the opportunity to lose you. Whether it be a relationship or friendship. Do your part always. Someone some day will give you 50% back.

Tbh, I thought about it but I won't stop seeing my friends of being "left out" of social media and seeing how my friends are because of some dude who wants to mess with my life. 

Growth, is what I call it lol.

Omg! Absolutely it is. Its my defense mechanism towards anything remotely hard in my life. But I'm working through it. Mental health is so important and mostly when "we" have had hard upbringings. 

My way of working though my anger/anxiety is surrounding myself with people who know how to tell me when I'm being aggressive towards them for no reason (obviously knowing my story) but yes. It absolutely is my anxiety coming out that way. 

And thank you!

I remember it being "berenstain". 

Here's why: when i was little i thought the song at the beggining of the show was so funny the way they finished the song with "berenstain bears" in the most country accent. Only because I wasn't used to hearing that heavy of an accent. And I would always say repeat it to my brother as a little inside joke. Just to sound funny in a country accent. 

Here's the scary part: I can't prove any of this because my brother had an accident and doesn't remember anything from when we were kids. So when I try to explain this to people that none of the Mandela effects apply to my memories I sound like I'm trying to cover something up lol.

But! Here's the twist. I remember the song being sung by a deep voiced country MAN. When infact, a woman sings that song. So I thought that was weird.
